title: 3 weeks into building an Unreal Engine 5.8 heavy-equipment & soil physics sim — 60s gameplay trailer + full breakdown of the AI pipeline (Claude Code, Antigravity/Gemini, ChatGPT, Tripo, Blender, ElevenLabs)
author: TechStandpoint
selftext:
Three days ago I posted a rough clip here asking if my Unreal Engine 5 construction sim was worth continuing. Honestly didn't expect 600+ upvotes and 70+ comments — between the encouragement and the actual operator/dev advice in that thread, you guys talked me into staying on it.



Spent the last few evenings after work tightening up the physics, fixing the digging, and putting together a clean 60-second in-engine cut (100% real UE 5.8 footage, no voiceover, zero ads/links).



\*\*What We Added & Tuned Since Last Post\*\*

\- \*\*Controls, ISO/SAE & Hydraulic Feel (shoutout to the operator comments):\*\* Added ISO/SAE pattern switching on gamepad, cylinder ramp times, shared pump flow (running boom + swing together shares flow instead of moving at full speed), JSON-tunable machine values, and bumped the excavator up to a 25-tonne LC class with real tipping limits.

\- \*\*Solid Boom/Bucket & Jump Turns:\*\* The boom, stick, cylinders, and grapple can't pass through undug ground anymore. Pushing Boom Down against the dirt lifts the front tracks in the air so you can counter-swing and walk the tracks around a planted bucket (jump turn) without tearing up turf.

\- \*\*Trench Digging, Hydrovac & Mat Physics:\*\* Deep bucket cuts now heave spoil into side ridges instead of piling up in front of the cab glass, and smoothed out crowd/curl so the bucket stops hopping. Rebuilt the hydrovac with a steady handheld wand (spinner + straight tips), dark wet mud in the hole, and \~20s per 2-ft section pace. Took dunnage off the flat-deck mat stack, made grapple jaws 3D-solid with real mat-nudge drag, and added inertia braking so a 991 kg mat stops swinging past the access road.

\- \*\*Tire Deflection & Truck Load Bounce:\*\* Added radial tire compression, leaf-spring heave/pitch/roll, and vehicle collisions — when a heaped bucket crashes into the dump box in the clip, the rear duals squat and the truck bounces on its springs.



\*\*Answers to the Main Questions From Last Thread\*\*

\- \*\*"How is the ground diggable everywhere?"\*\* One C++ layered heightfield soil subsystem (\~3 cm detail across topsoil, clay, sand, stony till) instead of voxels. Dirt is strictly conserved (bank -> loose -> compacted m³) and slumps to real slope angles.

\- \*\*"What does 'rigged in Blender' mean & how do joints/wheels move?"\*\* Whole-machine prompts make melted statues, so I generate 60+ separate sub-assemblies in Tripo (house, tracks, boom, stick, bucket, cab, beds — usually 2–4 tries when pin lugs melt), align pivots and build thin steel/timber parts via headless Blender 5.2 Python scripts, and drive every pin, cylinder, and wheel in UE 5.8 C++.

\- \*\*"How do you make the audio?"\*\* Generated the instrumental track and machine/Foley stems (birds, diesel, grapple clamp, mat thud, vacuum blower/water jet, bucket teeth, dirt hitting steel) in ElevenLabs, then beat-locked and mastered the cut (-14 LUFS) in Blender's VSE with Python/NumPy.

\- \*\*"How do you keep the code from turning into spaghetti?"\*\* 100% C++ and scripts (zero Blueprint graphs), strict markdown repo rules, and \*\*130 automated tests\*\* checking soil volume books and rig limits on every build. \*\*Claude (Ultra / Claude Code + Unreal MCP)\*\* does the heavy C++ lifting, \*\*Google Antigravity (Gemini)\*\* joined to orchestrate the cinema cameras, audio mastering, trailer physics fixes, and a private Cloudflare phone review page (so I can send notes from my phone), and \*\*ChatGPT\*\* helped early on (dropped Codex after one "ultra" run ate a week's quota in 7 hours).



Still plenty rough (no human drivers in the cabs yet!), but getting closer every night. Happy to answer anything else!
